output.summary: The PR changes inBounds from `index < length` to `index <= length`, introducing an off-by-one regression. The function now incorrectly returns true when index equals length, which is always out of bounds, and for empty collections (length 0) it returns true for index 0. This breaks the public contract that valid indices are 0 through length-1.

findings.title: Off-by-one: index equal to length is incorrectly reported in bounds
findings.body: The condition was changed from `index < length` to `index <= length`. For a collection of nonnegative integer length, valid indices are 0..length-1, so index === length is out of bounds. With the new operator, inBounds(3, 3) returns true (should be false), and inBounds(0, 0) returns true (empty collections have no valid index). This is a direct regression of the function's contract and causes out-of-bounds accesses to be accepted.
findings.evidence: src/bounds.ts line 2: `return index >= 0 && index <= length;`. Frozen counterexamples: {index:3,length:3} expected false, observed true; {index:0,length:0} expected false, observed true.
findings.suggestion: Restore the original strict comparison: `return index >= 0 && index < length;`

output.diagnosis: The PR replaced the strict `<` comparison with `<=`, so the first out-of-range index (index === length) and the empty-collection case (length 0, index 0) now evaluate as in bounds, violating the 0..length-1 contract.
